correctness.rationale: PASS. Normalize S² area and SO3 Haar as probability measures. For complex spherical harmonic Y_lm orthonormal on probability S², the k-th equatorial Fourier coefficient is zero except m=k and matching degree parity; the associated Legendre double-factorial expression, divided by representation dimension 2l+1, equals gamma(l,k)=[C(l+k,(l+k)/2) C(l-k,(l-k)/2)]/4^l. Schur orthogonality eliminates cross-degree terms in the SO3 rotation average. The measurement map is bounded L²(S²)->L²(SO3) by Jensen and Haar invariance, justifying extension from harmonic polynomials to continuous/L² data. Gamma(l,k)∼2/(pi l) for fixed k and parity. Mode 2 detects all even l>=2, mode5 all odd l>=5, leaving only 0,1,3; comparing positive gamma to (1+l(l+1))^(-1/2) yields two-sided H^(-1/2) equivalence, while unit even harmonics with l→∞ preclude any lower bound for s<1/2. For a support function, projection to P restricts h to P∩S² and translations alter only the first mode. Independent exact binomial arithmetic confirmed gamma(2,2)=3/8, gamma(4,2)=5/32, gamma(5,5)=63/256. Formula is analytically proven rather than inferred from three tests.
